newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: KLAIPEDOS NAFTA HANDLES LESS OIL IN MARCH.
newsitem.headline: KLAIPEDOS NAFTA HANDLES LESS OIL IN MARCH.

text.p: Lithuania's Klaipedos Nafta said on Wednesday it handled 28,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil less in March than in February although it more than doubled the volume during the first quarter versus the same priod in 1996.
"Klaipedos Nafta reloaded 266,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil in March versus 294,000 tonnes in February," director general of the company, Martinas Gusiatinas, told Reuters.
"During the first quarter of 1997, the company reloaded 772,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil versus 300,000 tonnes during the same period last year," Gusiatinas added.
Gusiatinas said the company did not operate for 10 days in March as Russian clients halted the transportation of loads as they were waiting for Russia's railway tariffs to be revised.
"The situation is complicated because heavy fuel transportation costs in Lithuania are higher than in Latvia and Estonia," Gusiatinas said.
"Klaipeda port's charges are also higher in Lithuania," he added.
He also said that the company could handle around 370,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil per month.
Some 46 percent of Klaipedos Nafta is owned by the state-run Naftos Terminals and 51 percent of the company's stake is in the hands of foreign investors.
